Repository coding-agent instructions. Follow `RULES.md` strictly; it is canonical for definition of done, formatting/lint, warnings-as-errors, tests/coverage, and code size/complexity budgets. `WORKFLOW.md` governs issues, branches, PRs, reviews, and merges. `RELEASING.md` governs releases, versioning, changelogs, tagging, and publishing. Repo tooling and explicit user instructions win conflicts.

For concrete requests, start with relevant files. Otherwise inspect top-level docs, manifests, and module READMEs. Do not assume module scope. Read every file you modify in full before editing. Do not remove, rename, or downgrade intentional functionality unless the user explicitly asked. Do not “fix” dependency or type problems by deleting behavior or weakening checks. Keep diffs tight; avoid unrelated refactors/formatting churn. Run repository validation commands after changes. Treat formatter, lint, warnings-as-errors, tests, and coverage as design constraints. Do not bypass hooks, checks, or validation steps. Never use `--no-verify`.

Never commit unless the user explicitly asks. If committing, commit only files changed in this session; use explicit paths; never broad staging; run `git status` and verify staged files. If related issue/PR, include `fixes #<number>` or `closes #<number>`. Commands:
`git add <specific-file-paths>`
`git pull --rebase`
`git reset --hard`
`git clean -fd`
`git commit --no-verify`

Protect other agents’ changes. Resolve conflicts only in files you changed. If conflict appears in untouched files, stop and ask user. Read full issues including comments. Analyze PRs before local changes. Do not open PRs, merge, or close anything unless explicitly asked. Keep responses concise, direct, technical. No emojis in commits, issues, PR comments, or code comments unless explicitly asked.

Store transient context under `.llm/{DIR}/`, choosing `{DIR}` to avoid collisions. Do not use `.context/`. Treat `.llm/` as disposable, untracked working state; promote durable documentation explicitly.
